name: vocabulary
title: Vocabulary
scope: A small study card for explaining a word in context and choosing one for an audience, not a full dictionary.
method: Read the word inside its sentence, not alone.
State the denotation, the literal meaning.
Note the connotation: positive, negative, or neutral.
Test a synonym and an antonym against that sentence.
Use context clues such as definition, example, contrast, or cause.
Choose the word that fits the audience and the purpose.

formulas.name: Synonym
formulas.expr: A synonym has a similar meaning; it is not always interchangeable.
formulas.use: Swap it in only if grammar, denotation, and tone still hold.

formulas.name: Near synonym
formulas.expr: A near synonym overlaps in meaning but can differ in strength or use.
formulas.use: Prefer the near synonym that matches the exact sense in this sentence.

formulas.name: Antonym
formulas.expr: An antonym has an opposite or clearly contrasting meaning.
formulas.use: Use the contrast to test whether the original sense was understood.

formulas.name: Denotation
formulas.expr: Denotation is the literal meaning, apart from feeling.
formulas.use: State this before discussing tone or persuasion.

formulas.name: Connotation
formulas.expr: Connotation is the feeling or association beyond the denotation.
formulas.use: Call it positive, negative, or neutral for this audience, not for all time.

formulas.name: Context clues
formulas.expr: A nearby definition, example, contrast, or cause can narrow a meaning.
formulas.use: Check the guess against the rest of the sentence before treating it as known.

formulas.name: Word choice
formulas.expr: Pick the word whose meaning and tone fit the audience and purpose.
formulas.use: A plainer or more formal near synonym is better when the first choice would mislead that reader.

checks: The synonym still fits the grammar and the tone of the sentence.
Denotation and connotation are stated separately.
A meaning guessed from context clues still fits the whole sentence.
The word choice matches the stated audience and purpose.
limits: This card is not a full dictionary and does not list every sense of a word.
A synonym or near synonym is not automatically interchangeable.
Connotation can change with the community and the context.
